method: Targeted rerun of the two line-edit cases after one change (the kept-words rule applies to cuts only; a line edit may join, split or smooth the writer's sentences in their own words) plus line rewrapping. Skill arm rerun on q03 and q07, 2 runs each, in fresh scratch folders via deploy.sh; no-skill outputs reused from the 2026-11-28 run. Blind judge per case. Agent-tool subagents, not the CLI harness; codex and grok not run.

known_gaps.q06-tenser-half: Deliberate, accepted by the owner: the skill reaches a named length with whole cuts and keeps the writer's words exactly, so it reads 'shorter more than tenser' to the judge (3.5 vs 4), where the baseline gains tension partly by inventing details. The owner's priority is the writer's own words.

notes: q03: rubric 1.0 both arms; judge 4.5 vs 4.5 (this judge rated the reused no-skill outputs 4 and 5, earlier judges 4 and 4); skill runs closer to the writer (similarity 0.91 vs 0.81) and added nothing. q07: one skilled run joined the stacked 'He was' sentences (5); the other again offered the join as a suggestion, this time on the ground that the stacking could be deliberate rather than citing the cut rule (4); 4.5 vs 5, unchanged from the previous run. The clause stopped the cut rule being cited for line edits, but the skill's 'ask when a choice could be deliberate' still leaves this one join unapplied in half the runs.
